metadata.network_profile: same Windows host/browser and aiortc loopback; real Beijing provider WAN; no TURN
metadata.client: headless Chromium, shipped RealtimeVoice and AudioWorklet
metadata.input_end_definition: last 10ms RMS>0.004 block in fixed synthetic WAV; AudioContext scheduled playback mapped to performance clock
metadata.cohort_rule: first planned quota of successful samples per case; extra identity setup retained separately; all attempts retained

notes: Actual shipped browser/aiortc, native understanding, business guard and Qwen TTS; local gateway with real cloud WAN.
Cross-process stages use minimum-RTT clock synchronization; RTT/2 is a network offset estimate, not a hard error bound.
Endpoint stage includes input transport, provider VAD and event return; provider internals cannot be separated.
Remote decoded PCM observed in browser is not a physical loudspeaker or trusted playback-completion proof.
A single candidate run cannot establish same-condition improvement or the relative P95/failure gate.
Stage P50 values must not be added to infer the end-to-end P50.
Clock implementation and resolution are recorded above; short stages below clock resolution do not mean zero work.

comparison_to_old_1621ms.note: Absolute P50 and observed numeric P95/failure targets passed; historical dates, WAN and knowledge/text differ, so strict same-condition improvement is not established.

shadow_timing_limitation: Initial isolation observer reused an already-set audio_started event for attempts 2-4; those onset timings are invalid and must not be used. All three complete candidates had text_matches=false; no candidate reached RTC. Observer subsequently corrected. Raw original results retained.
comparison_limits: Historical and current runs use the same fixed WAVs and browser measurement; WAN/provider conditions and dates are not identical.
Old 1.6s text length/knowledge version differ from v3; stage medians cannot be added or treated as causal attribution.
Synthetic fixed audio over localhost RTC plus real provider WAN does not validate physical microphone/speaker, TURN, packet loss or double talk.
Natural-pause recognition did not pass; semantic300 is not the delivery default.
Formal stable-profile failure rate and experimental-variant failures are reported separately, not erased or combined to claim a winner.
